description: Computer Knowledge - Computer Hardware question bank derived from FDA_SDA_Computer_Knowledge_18_2_Computer_Hardware.pdf. Covers introduction, CPU, motherboard, RAM, ROM, cache, HDD, SSD, input/output devices, storage devices and high-yield revision facts. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is computer hardware?

options.A: The set of programs and instructions that tells the computer what to do
options.B: The physical and tangible components of a computer system that can be seen or touched
options.C: Only the software stored on a hard disk
options.D: A type of cloud storage service

questions.explanation: Computer hardware refers to the physical and tangible components of a computer system that can be seen or touched, such as the CPU, motherboard, memory modules, keyboard, monitor and storage drives.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main category of computer hardware?

options.A: Processing components

questions.explanation: The main categories of computer hardware are processing components, memory components, input devices, output devices, storage devices and communication/networking devices. Operating system kernels are software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware is intangible; software is tangible
options.B: Hardware is the physical equipment; software is the set of programs and instructions that tells the hardware what to do
options.C: Hardware cannot store data; software can

questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical equipment of a computer, whereas software is the set of programs and instructions that tells the hardware what to do. They work together to perform computing tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a peripheral device?

options.A: A component inside the CPU that executes instructions
options.B: A hardware component connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions
options.D: A firmware chip on the motherboard

questions.explanation: A peripheral device is a hardware component connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions; examples include a keyboard, printer, external drive and scanner.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical port on a computer?

options.A: USB

questions.explanation: A port is a physical or logical connection point through which a computer communicates with another device. Examples of physical ports include USB, HDMI and Ethernet ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Central Processing Unit (CPU)?

options.A: The main printed circuit board of a computer
options.B: The main instruction-execution component that fetches, decodes, executes instructions and coordinates processing operations
options.C: A type of permanent storage device
options.D: An output device that displays information

questions.explanation: The CPU is the main instruction-execution component of a computer. It fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, executes them and coordinates processing operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the CPU commonly called the brain of the computer?

options.A: Because it is made of biological tissue
options.B: Because it executes program instructions and controls or coordinates the computer's processing activities
options.C: Because it stores all data permanently
options.D: Because it is the largest component of a computer

questions.explanation: The CPU is commonly called the brain of the computer because it executes program instructions and controls or coordinates the computer's processing activities. This is an analogy; other components also perform essential functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the principal components of a CPU commonly taught?

options.A: ALU, Control Unit and registers
options.D: Hard disk, SSD and USB drive

questions.explanation: The principal components commonly taught are the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU) and registers. Modern processors also contain caches, execution units, cores and other specialised components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the function of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)?

options.A: To fetch and decode instructions only
options.B: To perform arithmetic operations and logical or comparison operations
options.D: To convert digital signals to sound

questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, and logical or comparison operations such as AND, OR, NOT, greater than and equality.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the function of the Control Unit (CU)?

options.A: It performs arithmetic calculations only
options.B: It directs the operation of the processor, fetches and decodes instructions and coordinates data and control signals
options.C: It stores all active programs and data

questions.explanation: The Control Unit directs the operation of the processor. It fetches and decodes instructions and coordinates the movement of data and control signals among the CPU, memory and input/output components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are CPU registers?

options.A: Large-capacity secondary storage devices
options.B: Very small, extremely fast storage locations inside the processor that temporarily hold operands, addresses, instructions, status information and intermediate results
options.C: Slots on the motherboard for RAM modules

questions.explanation: Registers are very small, extremely fast storage locations inside the processor. They temporarily hold operands, addresses, instructions, status information and intermediate results needed during execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a processor core?

options.A: An individual instruction-execution unit within a CPU
options.C: A cooling fan for the CPU
options.D: A firmware chip on the motherboard

questions.explanation: A core is an individual instruction-execution unit within a CPU. A multicore processor contains two or more cores, allowing it to execute multiple instruction streams concurrently, subject to software and system constraints.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a single-core processor?

options.A: A processor with two or more cores
options.B: A processor with one processing core capable of executing instructions
options.D: A processor that cannot run an operating system

questions.explanation: A single-core processor has one processing core capable of executing instructions. It can still run multiple programs through operating-system scheduling, but it does not have multiple CPU cores.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a multicore processor?

options.A: A processor with one core
options.B: A processor containing two or more processing cores on one processor chip or package
options.C: A processor that uses magnetic tape for storage

questions.explanation: A multicore processor contains two or more processing cores on one processor chip or package; examples include dual-core, quad-core, hexa-core and octa-core processors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is clock speed in a CPU?

options.A: The number of instructions completed per second
options.B: The rate at which a processor's clock cycles occur, commonly measured in hertz (Hz), MHz or GHz

questions.explanation: Clock speed is the rate at which a processor's clock cycles occur, commonly measured in hertz (Hz), especially megahertz (MHz) or gigahertz (GHz). Clock speed alone does not determine total performance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does GHz mean when describing a CPU?

options.A: One billion cycles per second

questions.explanation: GHz means gigahertz; one gigahertz equals one billion cycles per second. A CPU's clock frequency is not the same as the number of instructions it completes per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the system bus?

options.A: A communication pathway that carries data, addresses or control signals between major computer components
options.B: A physical port for connecting printers

questions.explanation: A system bus is a communication pathway that carries data, addresses or control signals between major computer components. Traditional descriptions distinguish data, address and control buses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between a 32-bit and a 64-bit processor?

options.A: They refer to the width of certain registers and operations; a 64-bit architecture can address a much larger memory space

questions.explanation: The terms refer to the processor architecture and the width of certain registers and operations. A 64-bit architecture can address a much larger memory space than a 32-bit architecture, subject to operating-system and hardware limits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between CPU and GPU?

options.A: CPU is for graphics only; GPU is for general processing
options.B: CPU has a small number of powerful, flexible cores for general-purpose processing; GPU contains many parallel processing units optimised for graphics and highly parallel workloads
options.C: Both are identical in design and purpose
options.D: GPU cannot be used for AI or scientific computing

questions.explanation: A CPU is designed for general-purpose processing with a small number of powerful, flexible cores, while a GPU contains many parallel processing units optimised for graphics and other highly parallel workloads. GPUs are also used in AI and scientific computing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a heat sink in a computer?

options.A: A software program for cooling
options.B: A passive cooling component, usually made of metal with fins, that transfers heat away from a processor or other component

questions.explanation: A heat sink is a passive cooling component, usually made of metal with fins, that transfers heat away from a processor or other component to the surrounding air. A fan may be used with it to improve cooling.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is thermal throttling?

options.A: Increasing processor speed when it gets hot
options.B: Automatic reduction of a processor's operating frequency or performance when its temperature becomes too high
options.C: A method of cooling using liquid nitrogen

questions.explanation: Thermal throttling is the automatic reduction of a processor's operating frequency or performance when its temperature becomes too high, helping prevent overheating and damage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a motherboard?

options.A: The main printed circuit board (PCB) of a computer that provides physical connections and communication pathways for components

questions.explanation: A motherboard is the main printed circuit board (PCB) of a computer. It provides physical connections and communication pathways for the CPU, RAM, storage, expansion cards and peripheral interfaces.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the motherboard called the main circuit board?

options.A: Because it is the largest chip on the computer
options.B: Because many essential components connect to it and it provides the electrical and communication pathways that allow those components to work together
options.C: Because it contains the operating system
options.D: Because it is the only circuit board in a computer

questions.explanation: It is called the main circuit board because many essential components connect to it and it provides the electrical and communication pathways that allow those components to work together.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common feature found on a motherboard?

options.A: CPU socket

questions.explanation: Common motherboard features include the CPU socket, RAM slots, chipset or platform controller, expansion slots, storage connectors, power connectors, firmware chip, rear input/output ports and internal headers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a CPU socket?

options.A: A connector on the motherboard that holds and electrically connects a compatible processor
options.B: A slot for installing RAM modules
options.C: A port for connecting a monitor

questions.explanation: A CPU socket is the motherboard connector that holds and electrically connects a compatible processor to the motherboard. The processor and socket must be compatible.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are RAM slots on a motherboard?

options.A: Connectors into which memory modules are installed

questions.explanation: RAM slots are connectors into which memory modules are installed. They are commonly called DIMM slots on desktop systems and SO-DIMM slots on many laptops.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a chipset?

options.A: A group of controller circuitry or platform logic that manages communication between the processor and selected system devices
options.C: A cooling mechanism for the CPU

questions.explanation: A chipset is a group of controller circuitry or platform logic that manages communication between the processor and selected system devices. In modern computers, many functions once handled by a separate chipset are integrated into the CPU.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an expansion slot?

options.A: A motherboard connector that allows an additional card such as a graphics card, network card or sound card to be installed
options.C: A port for connecting a keyboard
options.D: A connector for the power supply unit

questions.explanation: An expansion slot is a motherboard connector that allows an additional card, such as a graphics card, network card or sound card, to be installed. PCI Express (PCIe) is the main modern expansion-slot standard for PCs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does BIOS stand for?

options.A: Basic Input/Output System

questions.explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input/Output System. It is traditional motherboard firmware that initialises hardware and starts the boot process.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is UEFI?

options.A: A modern firmware interface that initialises a computer's hardware and helps start the operating system, replacing or extending many functions of traditional BIOS

questions.explanation: UEFI stands for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface. It is a modern firmware interface that initialises a computer's hardware and helps start the operating system; it replaces or extends many functions of traditional BIOS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does UEFI stand for?

options.A: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface

questions.explanation: UEFI stands for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is CMOS in relation to a motherboard?

options.A: A type of CPU cache
options.B: In traditional PC terminology, firmware configuration data retained by a small battery-backed memory or equivalent non-volatile storage

questions.explanation: CMOS originally refers to Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor technology. In traditional PC terminology, CMOS settings commonly refers to firmware configuration data retained by a small battery-backed memory or equivalent non-volatile storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the function of the CMOS battery?

options.A: It powers the entire computer
options.B: It traditionally maintains the real-time clock and certain firmware settings when the computer is unplugged
options.C: It provides backup power to the RAM during normal operation

questions.explanation: The motherboard battery traditionally maintains the real-time clock and certain firmware settings when the computer is unplugged. Many newer systems store settings in non-volatile memory, so the exact role varies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a form factor of a motherboard?

options.A: Its physical dimensions, mounting points and some layout characteristics
options.B: The number of CPU cores it supports
options.C: The amount of RAM it can hold

questions.explanation: A motherboard form factor specifies its physical dimensions, mounting points and some layout characteristics. Common PC form factors include ATX, microATX and Mini-ITX.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common PC motherboard form factor?

options.A: ATX

questions.explanation: Common PC form factors include ATX, microATX and Mini-ITX. DDR4, NVMe and SATA are not motherboard form factors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the function of the motherboard power connector?

options.A: It receives electrical power from the power supply unit (PSU) and distributes it through motherboard power circuitry to system components
options.B: It connects the motherboard to the internet
options.C: It transfers data between the CPU and RAM
options.D: It connects the monitor to the motherboard

questions.explanation: The motherboard power connector receives electrical power from the power supply unit (PSU) and distributes it through motherboard power circuitry to system components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a motherboard and a CPU?

options.A: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects and supports components, whereas the CPU is the processor that executes instructions
options.B: The motherboard executes instructions, whereas the CPU connects components
options.D: The CPU is installed on the RAM

questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects and supports components, whereas the CPU is the processor that executes instructions. The CPU is installed on a compatible motherboard.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does RAM stand for?

options.A: Random Access Memory

questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It is the computer's main working memory, used to hold programs and data that are currently being used by the CPU.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is RAM called random access memory?

options.A: Because data is accessed sequentially
options.B: Because the processor can access any addressable memory location directly, rather than having to read locations sequentially
options.C: Because data is stored randomly on the disk
options.D: Because it can only be accessed randomly by the user

questions.explanation: It is called random access memory because the processor can access any addressable memory location directly, rather than having to read locations sequentially.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is main system RAM volatile or non-volatile?

options.A: Volatile

questions.explanation: Main system RAM is volatile memory, which means its contents are normally lost when power is switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main function of RAM?

options.A: To permanently store the operating system and files
options.B: To temporarily store the operating system, running programs and active data so that the CPU can access them much faster than secondary storage
options.C: To convert digital signals into sound
options.D: To provide a physical connection between the CPU and motherboard

questions.explanation: RAM temporarily stores the operating system, running programs and active data so that the CPU can access them much faster than it could access most secondary storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens when a computer has insufficient RAM?

options.A: The computer automatically shuts down permanently
options.B: The system may become slower because it has less space for active programs and may need to move data between RAM and storage using paging or swapping
options.D: The hard disk is automatically formatted

questions.explanation: The system may become slower because it has less space for active programs and may need to move data between RAM and storage using paging or swapping. This is much slower than accessing RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does DRAM stand for?

options.A: Dynamic Random Access Memory

questions.explanation: DRAM stands for Dynamic Random Access Memory. It stores each bit using a capacitor and transistor arrangement and must be periodically refreshed to retain data. It is commonly used as main system memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does DRAM store each bit, and why must it be refreshed?

options.A: Using a bistable circuit; it never needs refreshing
options.B: Using a capacitor and transistor arrangement; it must be periodically refreshed to retain data
options.C: Using magnetic platters; it needs no refresh
options.D: Using laser light; it needs no refresh

questions.explanation: DRAM stores each bit using a capacitor and transistor arrangement and must be periodically refreshed to retain data. It is commonly used as main system memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does SRAM stand for?

options.A: Static Random Access Memory

questions.explanation: SRAM stands for Static Random Access Memory. It stores data using a bistable circuit and does not require periodic refresh while power is supplied. It is faster and more expensive per bit than DRAM and is commonly used for CPU cache.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does SRAM store data?

options.A: Using a capacitor and transistor arrangement
options.B: Using a bistable circuit and it does not require periodic refresh while power is supplied

questions.explanation: SRAM stores data using a bistable circuit and does not require periodic refresh while power is supplied. It is faster and more expensive per bit than DRAM and is commonly used for CPU cache.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between SRAM and DRAM?

options.A: SRAM is generally faster, more expensive and does not need periodic refreshing; DRAM is denser and cheaper per bit but requires periodic refreshing
options.B: SRAM is slower and cheaper than DRAM
options.C: DRAM does not need refreshing while SRAM does
options.D: Both are identical in speed and cost

questions.explanation: SRAM is generally faster, more expensive and does not need periodic refreshing; DRAM is denser and cheaper per bit but requires periodic refreshing. SRAM is commonly used for cache, while DRAM is commonly used for main memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does DDR stand for in DDR RAM?

options.A: Double Data Rate

questions.explanation: DDR stands for Double Data Rate. DDR memory transfers data on both edges of the memory clock signal. Generations include DDR, DDR2, DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5; they differ in speed, voltage, design and compatibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does DDR memory transfer data?

options.A: On one edge of the memory clock signal only
options.B: On both edges of the memory clock signal
options.C: Only when the computer is switched off

questions.explanation: DDR memory transfers data on both edges of the memory clock signal. Generations include DDR, DDR2, DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can DDR4 RAM be installed in a DDR5 slot?

options.A: Yes, they are fully compatible
options.B: No, DDR4 and DDR5 modules use different electrical and physical specifications and are not interchangeable
options.D: Yes, if the computer is switched off

questions.explanation: No. DDR4 and DDR5 modules use different electrical and physical specifications and are not interchangeable in a motherboard slot.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does DIMM stand for?

options.A: Dual In-line Memory Module

questions.explanation: DIMM stands for Dual In-line Memory Module. It is a memory module format commonly used in desktop computers and servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does SO-DIMM stand for?

options.A: Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module
options.B: Standard Output Dual In-line Memory Module
options.C: Small Output Direct In-line Memory Module
options.D: Serial Outline Dual In-line Memory Module

questions.explanation: SO-DIMM stands for Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module. It is a smaller memory-module format commonly used in laptops and compact computers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Where is the SO-DIMM memory module format commonly used?

options.A: Desktop computers and servers

questions.explanation: SO-DIMM is a smaller memory-module format commonly used in laptops and compact computers. DIMM is commonly used in desktop computers and servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is RAM capacity commonly measured in?

options.A: Gigabytes (GB)

questions.explanation: RAM capacity is commonly measured in gigabytes (GB), such as 4 GB, 8 GB, 16 GB or 32 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does adding more RAM always make a computer faster?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No, more RAM can improve performance when the system was short of memory, but it may provide little benefit if existing RAM is already sufficient
options.C: No, adding RAM always slows down a computer

questions.explanation: No. More RAM can improve performance when the system was short of memory, but it may provide little benefit if existing RAM is already sufficient. CPU, storage, software and workload also affect performance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is dual-channel memory?

options.A: A memory configuration that uses two memory channels to increase the potential data bandwidth between the memory controller and RAM
options.B: A type of RAM that has two physical chips
options.C: A memory configuration that doubles the storage capacity automatically

questions.explanation: Dual-channel memory is a memory configuration that uses two memory channels to increase the potential data bandwidth between the memory controller and RAM. Correct module placement and platform support are required.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does ROM stand for?

options.A: Read Only Memory

questions.explanation: ROM stands for Read Only Memory. It is non-volatile memory used to retain firmware or other data when power is switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is ROM volatile or non-volatile?

options.A: Volatile

questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory because it retains stored contents without continuous electrical power.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main use of ROM in a computer?

options.A: To temporarily store running programs
options.B: To store firmware and essential startup instructions used to initialise hardware and begin the boot process

questions.explanation: ROM or ROM-like non-volatile memory stores firmware and essential startup instructions used to initialise hardware and begin the boot process.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does PROM stand for?

options.A: Programmable Read Only Memory

questions.explanation: PROM stands for Programmable Read Only Memory. It is supplied blank and can be programmed once by the user or manufacturer; after programming, its contents cannot normally be erased and rewritten.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about PROM is correct?

options.A: It can be erased using ultraviolet light
options.B: It is supplied blank and can be programmed once; after programming its contents cannot normally be erased and rewritten
options.C: It can be erased and rewritten electrically any number of times
options.D: It is a type of volatile RAM

questions.explanation: PROM is supplied blank and can be programmed once by the user or manufacturer; after programming, its contents cannot normally be erased and rewritten.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does EPROM stand for?

options.A: Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory

questions.explanation: EPROM stands for Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. Its contents can be erased using ultraviolet light and the chip can then be reprogrammed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How can the contents of an EPROM be erased?

options.A: Using ultraviolet light

questions.explanation: EPROM stands for Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. Its contents can be erased using ultraviolet light and the chip can then be reprogrammed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does EEPROM stand for?

options.A: Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
options.B: Extended Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
options.C: Electronic Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
options.D: External Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory

questions.explanation: EEPROM stands for Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. Its contents can be erased and rewritten electrically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How are the contents of an EEPROM erased and rewritten?

options.A: Using ultraviolet light
options.D: They cannot be erased at all

questions.explanation: EEPROM stands for Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory. Its contents can be erased and rewritten electrically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is flash memory?

options.A: A volatile memory used only as main RAM
options.B: A type of non-volatile semiconductor memory related to EEPROM technology, erased and written in blocks, used in USB drives, memory cards, SSDs and embedded devices

questions.explanation: Flash memory is a type of non-volatile semiconductor memory related to EEPROM technology. It is erased and written in blocks and is used in USB flash drives, memory cards, SSDs and many embedded devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?

options.A: RAM is generally volatile read/write working memory for active programs and data; ROM is non-volatile memory traditionally used to store firmware and data that must remain when power is off
options.B: RAM is non-volatile and ROM is volatile
options.D: ROM is used as main working memory and RAM stores firmware

questions.explanation: RAM is generally volatile read/write working memory used for active programs and data; ROM is non-volatile memory traditionally used to store firmware and data that must remain when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between PROM, EPROM and EEPROM?

options.A: PROM can generally be programmed only once; EPROM can be erased by ultraviolet light and reprogrammed; EEPROM can be erased and reprogrammed electrically
options.B: PROM can be erased electrically; EPROM only once; EEPROM by ultraviolet light
options.C: All three are identical in erasing method
options.D: None of them can be programmed

questions.explanation: PROM can generally be programmed only once; EPROM can be erased by ultraviolet light and reprogrammed; EEPROM can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is all ROM permanently unchangeable?

options.A: Yes, ROM can never be changed under any circumstances
options.B: No. PROM, EPROM and EEPROM variants can be programmed or erased under specified conditions, and modern firmware is commonly stored in reprogrammable flash memory
options.C: Yes, only RAM can be changed

questions.explanation: No. The term ROM is used broadly in computer fundamentals, but PROM, EPROM and EEPROM variants can be programmed or erased under specified conditions. Modern firmware is commonly stored in reprogrammable flash memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cache memory?

options.A: A small, very fast memory that stores copies of frequently or recently used instructions and data so the CPU can access them more quickly than from main memory

questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory that stores copies of frequently or recently used instructions and data so that the CPU can access them more quickly than from main memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is cache memory used?

options.A: To increase the storage capacity of the hard disk
options.B: To reduce the average time the CPU waits for data and instructions by keeping likely-needed information close to the processor
options.D: To connect the computer to the internet

questions.explanation: Cache memory reduces the average time the CPU waits for data and instructions by keeping likely-needed information close to the processor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Where is cache memory usually located in modern systems?

options.A: On the processor chip
options.D: Only on the motherboard's CMOS battery

questions.explanation: CPU cache is located on the processor chip in modern systems, although older designs sometimes used external cache. Some systems also use additional cache levels outside the CPU package.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the common levels of cache memory?

options.A: L1, L2 and L3

questions.explanation: The common levels are L1, L2 and L3. L1 is generally the smallest and fastest; L2 is usually larger and somewhat slower; L3 is often larger still and may be shared among CPU cores. Designs vary.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is L1 cache?

options.A: The smallest and generally fastest cache level, usually located within each CPU core, and may be divided into instruction cache and data cache
options.B: The largest and slowest cache level
options.C: A cache shared by all computers on a network

questions.explanation: L1 (Level 1) cache is the smallest and generally fastest cache level, usually located within each CPU core. It may be divided into instruction cache and data cache.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is L2 cache?

options.A: The smallest and fastest cache level
options.B: A cache level generally larger than L1 and usually slower, which may be dedicated to a core or arranged in another processor-specific configuration

questions.explanation: L2 (Level 2) cache is generally larger than L1 and usually slower. It may be dedicated to a core or arranged in another processor-specific configuration.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is L3 cache?

options.A: A cache level generally larger than L1 and L2 and often shared by multiple CPU cores
options.B: The smallest and fastest cache level
options.C: A cache located only on the hard disk

questions.explanation: L3 (Level 3) cache is generally larger than L1 and L2 and is often shared by multiple CPU cores, although exact designs vary by processor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which is faster: cache memory or RAM?

options.A: Cache memory is generally faster than main RAM
options.B: RAM is generally faster than cache memory
options.D: It depends only on the monitor used

questions.explanation: CPU cache is generally faster than main RAM, but it has much smaller capacity and is more expensive per unit of storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cache hit?

options.A: When the requested data or instruction is not found in the cache
options.B: When the requested data or instruction is found in the cache, allowing access without fetching it from a lower level of the memory hierarchy
options.C: When the cache is physically damaged
options.D: When the CPU is switched off

questions.explanation: A cache hit occurs when the requested data or instruction is found in the cache, allowing access without fetching it from a lower level of the memory hierarchy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cache miss?

options.A: When the requested data or instruction is found in the cache
options.B: When the requested data or instruction is not found in the cache, so it must be fetched from a lower level of memory or storage, causing additional delay
options.C: When the cache is full of data
options.D: When the CPU executes instructions too quickly

questions.explanation: A cache miss occurs when the requested data or instruction is not found in the cache, so it must be fetched from a lower level of memory or storage, causing additional delay.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between cache memory and RAM?

options.A: Cache is smaller and faster memory close to or inside the CPU that stores copies of frequently needed data; RAM is larger main memory that holds active programs and data
options.B: Cache is larger and slower than RAM
options.C: Both have the same capacity and speed
options.D: RAM is located inside the CPU and cache is on the hard disk

questions.explanation: Cache is smaller and faster memory close to or inside the CPU that stores copies of frequently needed data; RAM is larger main memory that holds active programs and data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hard disk drive (HDD)?

options.A: A non-volatile secondary storage device that stores digital data magnetically on rotating platters
options.B: A volatile memory used as main RAM
options.C: An output device that displays images

questions.explanation: A hard disk drive is a non-volatile secondary storage device that stores digital data magnetically on rotating platters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a main part of an HDD?

options.A: Magnetic platters

questions.explanation: A typical HDD contains one or more magnetic platters, a spindle motor, read/write heads, an actuator arm, controller electronics and a protective enclosure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does a hard disk drive store data?

options.A: By magnetising tiny regions on its rotating platters, which read/write heads access as the platters spin
options.B: By using laser light on optical discs
options.C: By storing electrical charges in flash memory cells

questions.explanation: An HDD stores data by magnetising tiny regions on its rotating platters. Read/write heads access the data as the platters spin.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a platter in an HDD?

options.A: A rigid circular disk coated with magnetic material on which data are stored
options.C: The power connector of the HDD

questions.explanation: A platter is a rigid circular disk coated with magnetic material on which data are stored.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a read/write head in an HDD?

options.A: The component that reads magnetic patterns from a platter and writes data by changing the magnetic state of regions on the platter
options.B: The motor that spins the platters
options.C: The cable that connects the HDD to the motherboard
options.D: The protective enclosure of the HDD

questions.explanation: A read/write head is the component that reads magnetic patterns from a platter and writes data by changing the magnetic state of regions on the platter.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spindle speed in an HDD?

options.A: The rotational speed of the HDD platters, measured in revolutions per minute (RPM)
options.B: The speed at which data is transferred over USB
options.C: The time taken to move the read/write head to a track
options.D: The amount of data stored on a platter

questions.explanation: Spindle speed is the rotational speed of the HDD platters, measured in revolutions per minute (RPM), such as 5,400 RPM or 7,200 RPM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does RPM stand for in hard disk specifications?

options.A: Revolutions Per Minute

questions.explanation: RPM stands for Revolutions Per Minute, the rotational speed of the HDD platters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is seek time in an HDD?

options.A: The time taken for the actuator to move the read/write head to the track containing the required data
options.B: The time taken to spin the platter to full speed
options.C: The time taken to format the disk
options.D: The time taken to transfer a file over the network

questions.explanation: Seek time is the time taken for the actuator to move the read/write head to the track containing the required data. It is one factor affecting HDD access time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an advantage of an HDD?

options.A: High storage capacity at a relatively low cost per gigabyte, useful for large files, backups and archives
options.D: Better resistance to physical shock than SSDs

questions.explanation: HDDs generally offer high storage capacity at a relatively low cost per gigabyte and are useful for storing large files, backups and archives.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of an HDD?

options.A: It contains moving mechanical parts, is generally slower than SSDs, can make noise and is more vulnerable to physical shock while operating
options.C: It is always more expensive per gigabyte than an SSD

questions.explanation: HDDs contain moving mechanical parts, are generally slower than SSDs, can make noise, consume more power in some use cases and are more vulnerable to physical shock while operating.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is disk fragmentation?

options.A: When parts of a file are stored in non-contiguous locations on a disk, which on HDDs can increase head movement and reduce performance
options.B: When a disk is physically broken into pieces

questions.explanation: Disk fragmentation occurs when parts of a file are stored in non-contiguous locations on a disk. On HDDs, this can increase head movement and reduce performance; SSDs are affected differently and should not be routinely defragmented using traditional HDD methods.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Should SSDs be routinely defragmented using traditional HDD methods?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No, SSDs are affected differently by fragmentation and should not be routinely defragmented using traditional HDD methods
options.C: Yes, but only once a day
options.D: Yes, but only when the SSD is full

questions.explanation: SSDs are affected differently by fragmentation and should not be routinely defragmented using traditional HDD methods. On HDDs, fragmentation can increase head movement and reduce performance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is formatting a hard disk?

options.A: Physically destroying the disk
options.B: Preparing a storage device or partition to store files by creating a file-system structure

questions.explanation: Formatting prepares a storage device or partition to store files by creating a file-system structure. Formatting can make existing data difficult to access, but a quick format does not necessarily secure all underlying data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does a quick format necessarily secure all underlying data?

options.A: Yes, quick format securely erases all data
options.B: No, a quick format does not necessarily secure all underlying data
options.D: Only if the disk is new

questions.explanation: Formatting can make existing data difficult to access, but a quick format does not necessarily secure all underlying data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Solid State Drive (SSD)?

options.A: A non-volatile storage device that stores data in flash memory chips and has no moving mechanical parts
options.B: A storage device that uses rotating magnetic platters

questions.explanation: An SSD is a non-volatile storage device that stores data in flash memory chips and has no moving mechanical parts.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does an SSD store data?

options.A: Magnetically on rotating platters
options.B: Electronically in NAND flash memory cells, managed by a controller that handles data placement, error correction, wear management and communication
options.C: Using laser light on optical discs

questions.explanation: An SSD stores data electronically in NAND flash memory cells. A controller manages data placement, error correction, wear management and communication with the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a main advantage of an SSD over an HDD?

options.A: Faster access and data transfer, lower latency, silent operation, lower power use in many cases and better resistance to physical shock

questions.explanation: SSDs generally provide faster access and data transfer, lower latency, silent operation, lower power use in many cases and better resistance to physical shock because they have no moving platters or heads.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of an SSD?

options.A: They usually cost more per gigabyte than HDDs, have finite write endurance, and data recovery after certain controller or flash failures can be difficult
options.C: They make loud noise during operation
options.D: They are always slower than HDDs

questions.explanation: SSDs usually cost more per gigabyte than HDDs, have finite write endurance, and data recovery after certain controller or flash failures can be difficult. Capacity and endurance vary by model and technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is NAND flash memory?

options.A: A type of non-volatile semiconductor memory used in SSDs, USB drives and memory cards, storing data in cells and organised into pages and blocks

questions.explanation: NAND flash is a type of non-volatile semiconductor memory used in SSDs, USB drives and memory cards. It stores data in cells and is organised into pages and blocks for reading, writing and erasing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a SATA SSD?

options.A: An SSD that connects through the Serial ATA interface, commonly using a 2.5-inch drive form factor, with speed limited by the SATA interface
options.B: An SSD that connects directly to the CPU socket
options.C: An SSD that uses magnetic platters
options.D: An SSD that requires no interface

questions.explanation: A SATA SSD connects through the Serial ATA interface, commonly using a 2.5-inch drive form factor. Its speed is limited by the SATA interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an NVMe SSD?

options.A: An SSD that uses the Non-Volatile Memory Express protocol, typically over PCI Express (PCIe), to communicate with flash storage
options.B: An SSD that uses the SATA interface only

questions.explanation: An NVMe SSD uses the Non-Volatile Memory Express protocol, typically over PCI Express (PCIe), to communicate with flash storage. It can provide much higher performance and lower latency than SATA-based storage, depending on the model and connection.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does NVMe stand for?

options.A: Non-Volatile Memory Express

questions.explanation: NVMe stands for Non-Volatile Memory Express.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between SATA and NVMe?

options.A: SATA is an older storage interface/protocol family originally designed for disk drives, while NVMe is a protocol designed for non-volatile memory and commonly operates over PCIe; NVMe SSDs can offer substantially higher throughput and lower latency
options.B: SATA is faster than NVMe in all cases
options.C: NVMe is an older interface than SATA

questions.explanation: SATA is an older storage interface/protocol family originally designed for disk drives, while NVMe is a protocol designed for non-volatile memory and commonly operates over PCIe. NVMe SSDs can offer substantially higher throughput and lower latency.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an M.2 SSD?

options.A: A physical form factor and connector specification for internal expansion devices, including SSDs; an M.2 drive may use SATA or PCIe/NVMe
options.B: A protocol that always means NVMe

questions.explanation: M.2 is a physical form factor and connector specification for internal expansion devices, including SSDs. An M.2 drive may use SATA or PCIe/NVMe; M.2 does not automatically mean NVMe.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between M.2 and NVMe?

options.A: M.2 describes a physical form factor/connector, whereas NVMe describes a storage communication protocol; an M.2 SSD can use SATA or NVMe
options.B: M.2 is a protocol and NVMe is a form factor
options.D: M.2 is always faster than NVMe

questions.explanation: M.2 describes a physical form factor/connector, whereas NVMe describes a storage communication protocol. An M.2 SSD can use SATA or NVMe, depending on the drive and motherboard support.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is wear levelling in an SSD?

options.A: A controller technique that distributes write and erase operations across flash memory cells to reduce uneven wear and extend the SSD's usable life
options.B: A method of physically levelling the SSD on a desk
options.C: A technique to increase the SSD's physical weight

questions.explanation: Wear levelling is a controller technique that distributes write and erase operations across flash memory cells to reduce uneven wear and extend the SSD's usable life.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is TRIM in an SSD?

options.A: A command by which an operating system informs an SSD which data blocks are no longer needed, allowing the SSD controller to manage free space and maintain performance more efficiently
options.B: A method of physically trimming the SSD casing
options.C: A type of flash memory cell

questions.explanation: TRIM is a command by which an operating system informs an SSD which data blocks are no longer needed, allowing the SSD controller to manage free space and maintain performance more efficiently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally faster: HDD or SSD?

options.A: An SSD is generally faster than an HDD, particularly for random access and operating-system startup, because it has no mechanical seek time
options.B: An HDD is generally faster than an SSD
options.C: Both are exactly equal in speed
options.D: It depends only on the monitor

questions.explanation: An SSD is generally faster than an HDD, particularly for random access and operating-system startup, because it has no mechanical seek time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can an SSD lose data when power is switched off?

options.A: An SSD is non-volatile and is designed to retain data without power, but data retention is not unlimited and depends on factors such as flash wear, temperature, age and device condition
options.B: Yes, an SSD loses all data immediately when power is switched off
options.C: No, SSD data retention is guaranteed forever
options.D: Only if the SSD is new

questions.explanation: An SSD is non-volatile and is designed to retain data without power, but data retention is not unlimited and depends on factors such as flash wear, temperature, age and device condition.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an input device?

options.A: A hardware component used to enter data, instructions or control signals into a computer
options.B: A component that displays output on a screen

questions.explanation: An input device is a hardware component used to enter data, instructions or control signals into a computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a keyboard?

options.A: An input device containing keys used to enter letters, numbers, symbols and commands into a computer
options.B: An output device that displays text

questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device containing keys used to enter letters, numbers, symbols and commands into a computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are main groups of keys on a keyboard?

options.A: Alphanumeric keys, function keys, modifier keys, navigation keys, editing keys, arrow keys and the numeric keypad

questions.explanation: Common groups include alphanumeric keys, function keys, modifier keys such as Shift/Ctrl/Alt, navigation keys, editing keys, arrow keys and the numeric keypad. Layouts vary.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mouse?

options.A: A pointing input device used to move a pointer on the screen and perform actions such as clicking, selecting, dragging and scrolling
options.B: An output device that produces sound

questions.explanation: A mouse is a pointing input device used to move a pointer on the screen and perform actions such as clicking, selecting, dragging and scrolling.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does an optical mouse detect movement?

options.A: Using light, commonly from an LED or laser-based optical system, and a sensor to detect movement across a surface

questions.explanation: An optical mouse uses light, commonly from an LED or laser-based optical system, and a sensor to detect movement across a surface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a trackball?

options.A: A pointing device in which the user rotates an exposed ball with fingers or a thumb to move the on-screen pointer while the device itself remains stationary
options.B: A device that projects images onto a wall

questions.explanation: A trackball is a pointing device in which the user rotates an exposed ball with fingers or a thumb to move the on-screen pointer while the device itself remains stationary.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a touchpad?

options.A: A touch-sensitive pointing surface commonly built into laptops and used to control the pointer through finger movement and gestures

questions.explanation: A touchpad is a touch-sensitive pointing surface commonly built into laptops and used to control the pointer through finger movement and gestures.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a scanner?

options.A: An input device that captures text, photographs or other printed images and converts them into digital image data
options.B: An output device that prints documents

questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device that captures text, photographs or other printed images and converts them into digital image data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does OCR stand for?

options.A: Optical Character Recognition

questions.explanation: OCR stands for Optical Character Recognition. It is technology that recognises printed or handwritten characters in an image and converts them into machine-readable text; accuracy depends on image quality and the text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is OCR technology used for?

options.A: Recognising printed or handwritten characters in an image and converting them into machine-readable text
options.B: Detecting shaded marks on answer sheets
options.C: Reading magnetic-ink characters on bank cheques

questions.explanation: OCR is technology that recognises printed or handwritten characters in an image and converts them into machine-readable text; accuracy depends on image quality and the text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is OMR used for?

options.A: Detecting marked areas on specially designed forms, such as shaded bubbles on objective examination answer sheets
options.B: Recognising printed characters in an image
options.C: Reading magnetic-ink characters on bank cheques

questions.explanation: OMR stands for Optical Mark Recognition. It detects marked areas on specially designed forms, such as shaded bubbles on objective examination answer sheets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device is used to read answer-sheet bubbles in many objective examinations?

options.A: An OMR reader

questions.explanation: An OMR reader is used to detect shaded responses on specially designed objective examination answer sheets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does MICR stand for?

options.A: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition

questions.explanation: MICR stands for Magnetic Ink Character Recognition. It reads characters printed using magnetic ink, especially on bank cheques, to support automated processing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device is used to read characters printed on bank cheques?

options.A: A MICR reader

questions.explanation: A MICR reader is used to read magnetic-ink characters printed on bank cheques.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between OCR, OMR and MICR?

options.A: OCR recognises characters from printed or handwritten images; OMR detects marked positions on forms; MICR reads characters printed with magnetic ink, especially on bank cheques
options.B: OCR detects marks; OMR reads magnetic ink; MICR recognises characters
options.C: All three perform exactly the same function
options.D: OMR recognises characters; OCR reads magnetic ink; MICR detects marks

questions.explanation: OCR recognises characters from printed or handwritten images; OMR detects marked positions on forms; MICR reads characters printed with magnetic ink, especially on bank cheques.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a barcode reader?

options.A: An input device that scans a printed barcode and converts its encoded pattern into digital data, commonly used in retail, libraries and inventory systems
options.B: An output device that prints barcodes
options.D: A device that reads magnetic-ink characters on cheques

questions.explanation: A barcode reader is an input device that scans a printed barcode and converts its encoded pattern into digital data, commonly used in retail, libraries and inventory systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a QR code reader?

options.A: A device that captures and decodes a two-dimensional Quick Response code, which can contain text, identifiers or a web address
options.B: A device that prints QR codes
options.C: A device that reads magnetic-ink characters
options.D: A type of optical disc drive

questions.explanation: A QR code reader captures and decodes a two-dimensional Quick Response code, which can contain text, identifiers or a web address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a microphone?

options.A: An input device that converts sound waves into electrical or digital signals for recording, communication and voice input
options.B: An output device that produces sound

questions.explanation: A microphone is an input device that converts sound waves into electrical or digital signals for recording, communication and voice input.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a webcam?

options.A: A digital camera used as an input device to capture still images or video for video calls, recording and other applications
options.B: An output device that projects images

questions.explanation: A webcam is a digital camera used as an input device to capture still images or video for video calls, recording and other applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a joystick?

options.A: A pointing or control input device with a movable stick used to control movement or direction, commonly in games, simulators and specialised machinery
options.B: An output device that produces sound

questions.explanation: A joystick is a pointing or control input device with a movable stick used to control movement or direction, commonly in games, simulators and specialised machinery.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a light pen?

options.A: A pen-shaped pointing device that detects its position on a compatible display, used with older display technologies and now largely obsolete
options.B: A pen that stores data permanently
options.C: A device that prints text on paper

questions.explanation: A light pen is a pen-shaped pointing device that detects its position on a compatible display. It was used with older display technologies and is largely obsolete.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a graphics tablet or digitiser?

options.A: An input device that allows a user to draw or write with a stylus and transfer the movements into digital form
options.B: An output device that displays images

questions.explanation: A graphics tablet is an input device that allows a user to draw or write with a stylus and transfer the movements into digital form.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device functions as both an input device and an output device?

options.A: A touchscreen

questions.explanation: A touchscreen is a display that also accepts touch input. It functions as both an input device and an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a biometric input device?

options.A: A device that captures a measurable human characteristic, such as a fingerprint, face pattern, iris pattern or voice, for identification or authentication
options.B: A device that measures computer temperature
options.C: A device that prints biometric data
options.D: A storage device for biometric data

questions.explanation: A biometric input device captures a measurable human characteristic, such as a fingerprint, face pattern, iris pattern or voice, for identification or authentication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a fingerprint scanner?

options.A: A device that captures fingerprint ridge patterns and converts them into digital information for comparison during identity verification
options.B: A device that prints fingerprints on paper

questions.explanation: A fingerprint scanner captures fingerprint ridge patterns and converts them into digital information for comparison during identity verification.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a sensor as an input device?

options.A: A device that detects a physical condition, such as temperature, light, pressure, motion or humidity, and provides a signal that a computer or controller can process
options.B: A device that displays output on a screen

questions.explanation: A sensor detects a physical condition, such as temperature, light, pressure, motion or humidity, and provides a signal that a computer or controller can process.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an output device?

options.A: A hardware component that presents processed information from a computer to the user or to another system
options.B: A component used to enter data into a computer

questions.explanation: An output device is a hardware component that presents processed information from a computer to the user or to another system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a monitor?

options.A: An output device that displays text, images, video and graphical information on a screen
options.B: An input device used to type text

questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device that displays text, images, video and graphical information on a screen.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a pixel?

options.A: The smallest addressable unit of a digital image or display

questions.explanation: A pixel, or picture element, is the smallest addressable unit of a digital image or display. A screen's resolution is commonly expressed as the number of pixels across and down.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is screen resolution?

options.A: The number of pixels displayed horizontally and vertically, such as 1920 × 1080
options.B: The physical size of the monitor in inches
options.D: The refresh rate of the monitor

questions.explanation: Screen resolution is the number of pixels displayed horizontally and vertically, such as 1920 × 1080. Higher resolution can provide more image detail, subject to screen size and content.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does LCD stand for?

options.A: Liquid Crystal Display

questions.explanation: LCD stands for Liquid Crystal Display. An LCD uses liquid crystals to control light from a backlight or, in some designs, another illumination system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an LED monitor in common terminology?

options.A: An LCD monitor that uses light-emitting diodes as its backlight
options.B: A display made entirely from LED pixels

questions.explanation: In common monitor terminology, an LED monitor is an LCD monitor that uses light-emitting diodes as its backlight. It is not necessarily a display made entirely from LED pixels.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does OLED stand for?

options.A: Organic Light-Emitting Diode

questions.explanation: OLED stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. Each pixel produces its own light, allowing deep blacks and high contrast because individual pixels can be switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a key advantage of an OLED display?

options.A: Each pixel produces its own light, allowing deep blacks and high contrast because individual pixels can be switched off
options.B: It requires a separate backlight for every pixel

questions.explanation: OLED stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. Each pixel produces its own light, allowing deep blacks and high contrast because individual pixels can be switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a printer?

options.A: An output device that produces a physical copy of digital text or images on paper or another medium
options.B: An input device that scans documents

questions.explanation: A printer is an output device that produces a physical copy of digital text or images on paper or another medium; the printed output is called a hard copy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hard copy?

options.A: A physical, usually printed, representation of information, such as a printed document or photograph
options.C: A file stored on a USB drive

questions.explanation: A hard copy is a physical, usually printed, representation of information, such as a printed document or photograph.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a soft copy?

options.A: An electronic or digital version of information that can be viewed or stored on a computer, such as a PDF file or document

questions.explanation: A soft copy is an electronic or digital version of information that can be viewed or stored on a computer, such as a PDF file or document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the two broad categories of printers?

options.A: Impact printers and non-impact printers

questions.explanation: Printers are broadly classified as impact printers and non-impact printers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an impact printer?

options.A: A printer that prints by mechanically striking an inked ribbon against paper
options.B: A printer that sprays liquid ink droplets
options.C: A printer that uses toner and a laser
options.D: A printer that uses heat-sensitive paper only

questions.explanation: An impact printer prints by mechanically striking an inked ribbon against paper. Examples include dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a dot-matrix printer?

options.A: An impact printer that forms characters and images from patterns of dots produced by pins striking an inked ribbon
options.B: A non-impact printer that sprays ink droplets

questions.explanation: A dot-matrix printer is an impact printer that forms characters and images from patterns of dots produced by pins striking an inked ribbon.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which printer uses pins to strike an inked ribbon?

options.A: A dot-matrix printer

questions.explanation: A dot-matrix printer uses pins to strike an inked ribbon. It is an impact printer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a daisy-wheel printer?

options.A: An impact printer that uses a wheel with raised characters; a selected character strikes an inked ribbon to print the character
options.B: A non-impact printer that sprays ink droplets

questions.explanation: A daisy-wheel printer is an impact printer that uses a wheel with raised characters; a selected character strikes an inked ribbon to print the character.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a line printer?

options.A: An impact printer that prints an entire line of text at a time and is designed for high-volume printing
options.B: A printer that prints one character per minute

questions.explanation: A line printer is an impact printer that prints an entire line of text at a time and is designed for high-volume printing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a non-impact printer?

options.A: A printer that produces output without mechanically striking an inked ribbon against paper
options.B: A printer that uses pins to strike an inked ribbon
options.C: A printer that requires carbon paper
options.D: A printer that only prints in black and white

questions.explanation: A non-impact printer produces output without mechanically striking an inked ribbon against paper. Examples include inkjet and laser printers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an inkjet printer?

options.A: A non-impact printer that creates text and images by spraying tiny droplets of liquid ink onto paper
options.B: An impact printer that uses pins
options.C: A printer that uses toner and a laser
options.D: A printer that uses heat-sensitive paper only

questions.explanation: An inkjet printer is a non-impact printer that creates text and images by spraying tiny droplets of liquid ink onto paper.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which printer commonly uses liquid ink droplets?

options.A: An inkjet printer

questions.explanation: An inkjet printer uses tiny droplets of liquid ink.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a laser printer?

options.A: A non-impact printer that uses an electro-photographic process, a laser or LED imaging system and toner to produce printed output
options.B: An impact printer that uses pins
options.C: A printer that sprays liquid ink
options.D: A printer that uses heat-sensitive paper only

questions.explanation: A laser printer is a non-impact printer that uses an electro-photographic process, a laser or LED imaging system and toner to produce printed output.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which printer uses toner?

options.A: A laser printer

questions.explanation: A laser printer uses toner, a fine powder, to form printed images on paper.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a thermal printer?

options.A: A printer that uses heat to create an image on heat-sensitive paper or to transfer ink from a ribbon, commonly used for receipts, labels and tickets
options.B: A printer that uses a laser and toner
options.C: A printer that uses pins and an inked ribbon
options.D: A printer that sprays liquid ink droplets

questions.explanation: A thermal printer uses heat to create an image on heat-sensitive paper or to transfer ink from a ribbon. It is commonly used for receipts, labels and tickets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a plotter?

options.A: An output device used to produce large, precise drawings, maps, engineering plans and designs; modern large-format plotters may use inkjet technology
options.B: An input device used to scan documents
options.C: A storage device for engineering files

questions.explanation: A plotter is an output device used to produce large, precise drawings, maps, engineering plans and designs. Modern large-format plotters may use inkjet technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a projector?

options.A: An output device that displays computer-generated images or video on a larger screen or surface for presentations and group viewing
options.B: An input device that captures images

questions.explanation: A projector is an output device that displays computer-generated images or video on a larger screen or surface for presentations and group viewing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are speakers?

options.A: Audio output devices that convert electrical or digital audio signals into sound that can be heard by users

questions.explanation: Speakers are audio output devices that convert electrical or digital audio signals into sound that can be heard by users.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between impact and non-impact printers?

options.A: Impact printers print by physically striking an inked ribbon against paper; non-impact printers produce output without this mechanical striking action
options.B: Impact printers use toner; non-impact printers use pins
options.C: Impact printers are always laser-based; non-impact printers are always dot-matrix

questions.explanation: Impact printers print by physically striking an inked ribbon against paper; non-impact printers produce output without this mechanical striking action. Dot-matrix is impact, while inkjet and laser are non-impact.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which printer is commonly suitable for multi-copy forms using carbon paper?

options.A: An impact printer, particularly a dot-matrix printer, because its pins strike the paper and ribbon

questions.explanation: An impact printer, particularly a dot-matrix printer, can print through multi-part forms because its pins strike the paper and ribbon.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a storage device?

options.A: Hardware used to record, retain and retrieve digital data, instructions and information
options.B: A device that displays output on a screen
options.C: A device that enters data into a computer
options.D: A firmware chip on the motherboard

questions.explanation: A storage device is hardware used to record, retain and retrieve digital data, instructions and information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How is computer storage commonly divided?

options.A: Primary storage, such as RAM and cache, and secondary storage, such as HDDs, SSDs, optical discs and USB flash drives
options.B: Only into input and output storage
options.C: Only into hardware and software storage
options.D: Only into local and network storage

questions.explanation: Computer storage is commonly divided into primary storage, such as RAM and cache, and secondary storage, such as HDDs, SSDs, optical discs and USB flash drives. Some classifications also discuss tertiary or offline archival storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is primary storage?

options.A: Memory directly accessible by the CPU or closely integrated with processing, such as registers, cache and main memory; generally faster and lower capacity than secondary storage
options.B: Long-term archival storage such as magnetic tape

questions.explanation: Primary storage is memory directly accessible by the CPU or closely integrated with processing, such as registers, cache and main memory. It is generally faster and has lower capacity than secondary storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is secondary storage?

options.A: Non-volatile storage used to retain programs and data for long-term use, such as HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, memory cards and optical discs

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile storage used to retain programs and data for long-term use, such as HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, memory cards and optical discs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is tertiary storage?

options.A: Storage used for large-scale archival or backup purposes, often involving removable media libraries or automated tape systems, and generally slower to access than primary and ordinary secondary storage

questions.explanation: Tertiary storage is storage used for large-scale archival or backup purposes, often involving removable media libraries or automated tape systems. It is generally slower to access than primary and ordinary secondary storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is magnetic storage?

options.A: Storage that records data by changing magnetic states on a medium, with examples including hard disk drives and magnetic tape
options.B: Storage that uses laser light to read or write data
options.C: Storage that uses flash memory cells
options.D: Storage that uses cloud servers only

questions.explanation: Magnetic storage records data by changing magnetic states on a medium. Examples include hard disk drives and magnetic tape.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is optical storage?

options.A: Storage that uses laser light to read or write data on optical media, such as CD, DVD and Blu-ray Disc
options.C: Storage that uses NAND flash memory
options.D: Storage that uses cloud servers only

questions.explanation: Optical storage uses laser light to read or write data on optical media. Examples include CD, DVD and Blu-ray Disc.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does CD stand for?

options.A: Compact Disc

questions.explanation: CD stands for Compact Disc. It is an optical storage medium commonly used for digital audio and data; a standard CD commonly stores about 700 MB of data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Approximately how much data does a standard CD commonly store?

options.A: About 700 MB

questions.explanation: A standard CD commonly stores about 700 MB of data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
