questions.question: What does DVD stand for?

options.A: Digital Versatile Disc

questions.explanation: DVD stands for Digital Versatile Disc (also historically called Digital Video Disc). A common single-layer, single-sided DVD stores about 4.7 GB; capacities vary by type and layer count.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How much data does a common single-layer, single-sided DVD store?

options.A: About 4.7 GB

questions.explanation: A common single-layer, single-sided DVD stores about 4.7 GB; capacities vary by type and layer count.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What type of laser does a Blu-ray Disc use?

options.A: A blue-violet laser

questions.explanation: Blu-ray Disc is an optical storage format that uses a blue-violet laser. A standard single-layer disc commonly stores 25 GB, while dual-layer discs commonly store 50 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How much data does a standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly store?

options.A: 25 GB

questions.explanation: A standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly stores 25 GB, while dual-layer discs commonly store 50 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How much data does a dual-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly store?

options.A: 50 GB

questions.explanation: A standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly stores 25 GB, while dual-layer discs commonly store 50 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which optical disc format commonly stores the most data among CD, DVD and standard single-layer Blu-ray?

options.A: A standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc (25 GB)

questions.explanation: A standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly stores 25 GB, more than a typical DVD (4.7 GB) or CD (about 700 MB).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is magnetic tape storage?

options.A: A sequential-access storage medium commonly used for backups and long-term archival storage because it can provide high capacity at a relatively low cost per unit
options.B: A random-access storage medium used for main memory
options.C: An optical storage medium read by laser

questions.explanation: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access storage medium commonly used for backups and long-term archival storage because it can provide high capacity at a relatively low cost per unit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a USB flash drive?

options.A: A small portable storage device that uses flash memory and connects through a Universal Serial Bus (USB) interface
options.B: A storage device that uses magnetic platters

questions.explanation: A USB flash drive is a small portable storage device that uses flash memory and connects through a Universal Serial Bus (USB) interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does USB stand for?

options.A: Universal Serial Bus

questions.explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a memory card?

options.A: A small removable flash-storage device used in cameras, phones, portable devices and other equipment, with common formats including SD and microSD

questions.explanation: A memory card is a small removable flash-storage device used in cameras, phones, portable devices and other equipment. Common formats include SD and microSD.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud storage?

options.A: A service in which data are stored on remote servers and accessed over a network, usually the internet, with the provider managing the underlying storage infrastructure
options.B: A physical storage device owned by the user

questions.explanation: Cloud storage is a service in which data are stored on remote servers and accessed over a network, usually the internet. The provider manages the underlying storage infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is cloud storage a physical storage device?

options.A: No, cloud storage is a storage service or model, not a single physical device owned by the user; the data ultimately reside on physical storage systems in data centres
options.B: Yes, it is a single physical hard disk owned by the user
options.C: Yes, it is a type of USB drive
options.D: Yes, it is a type of RAM

questions.explanation: No. Cloud storage is a storage service or model, not a single physical device owned by the user. The data ultimately reside on physical storage systems in data centres.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between HDD and SSD?

options.A: An HDD stores data magnetically on rotating platters and uses moving heads; an SSD stores data in flash memory and has no moving parts; SSDs are generally faster while HDDs often offer lower cost per gigabyte
options.B: An HDD uses flash memory and an SSD uses magnetic platters
options.D: An SSD uses optical discs and an HDD uses magnetic tape

questions.explanation: An HDD stores data magnetically on rotating platters and uses moving heads; an SSD stores data in flash memory and has no moving parts. SSDs are generally faster, while HDDs often offer lower cost per gigabyte.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a USB flash drive and an external HDD?

options.A: Both are portable secondary storage devices; a USB flash drive uses flash memory and is compact, while an external HDD uses magnetic rotating platters and often offers high capacity at a lower cost per gigabyte
options.B: A USB flash drive uses magnetic platters and an external HDD uses flash memory
options.D: A USB flash drive is not a storage device

questions.explanation: Both are portable secondary storage devices. A USB flash drive uses flash memory and is compact; an external HDD uses magnetic rotating platters and often offers high capacity at a lower cost per gigabyte.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a backup?

options.A: A separate copy of data kept so that the data can be restored after accidental deletion, corruption, hardware failure, theft or another loss event
options.C: A method of increasing CPU speed

questions.explanation: A backup is a separate copy of data kept so that the data can be restored after accidental deletion, corruption, hardware failure, theft or another loss event.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between storage capacity and storage speed?

options.A: Storage capacity is the amount of data a device can hold, commonly measured in bytes; storage speed describes how quickly data can be read or written, commonly measured in MB/s or GB/s, along with access latency
options.B: Storage capacity is measured in MB/s and storage speed in bytes
options.C: Both terms mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Storage speed is measured only in pixels

questions.explanation: Storage capacity is the amount of data a device can hold, commonly measured in bytes; storage speed describes how quickly data can be read or written, commonly measured in MB/s or GB/s, along with access latency.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is sequential access?

options.A: Data are accessed in a sequence, where reaching a particular item may require passing earlier items; magnetic tape is a common example
options.B: Any location can be accessed directly without reading preceding locations
options.C: Data are accessed only through the cloud
options.D: Data are accessed only by the CPU registers

questions.explanation: Sequential access means data are accessed in a sequence, where reaching a particular item may require passing earlier items. Magnetic tape is a common example.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is direct or random access?

options.A: A storage system can access a specified location without reading all preceding locations; RAM and disk-based storage support direct access, although their access times differ
options.B: Data must be read in strict sequence from the beginning
options.C: Data can only be accessed via magnetic tape
options.D: Data can only be accessed by the operating system

questions.explanation: Direct or random access means a storage system can access a specified location without reading all preceding locations. RAM and disk-based storage support direct access, although their access times differ.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between read speed and write speed?

options.A: Read speed measures how quickly a device retrieves data; write speed measures how quickly it records data; the two speeds may differ and depend on workload, device design and interface
options.B: Read speed measures writing and write speed measures reading
options.D: Read speed is measured in pixels

questions.explanation: Read speed measures how quickly a device retrieves data; write speed measures how quickly it records data. The two speeds may differ and depend on workload, device design and interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does data transfer rate mean?

options.A: The amount of data transferred per unit of time, commonly expressed in bits per second (bps) or bytes per second (B/s) and their multiples
options.B: The total capacity of a storage device
options.C: The physical size of a storage device
options.D: The number of files stored on a device

questions.explanation: Data transfer rate is the amount of data transferred per unit of time, commonly expressed in bits per second (bps) or bytes per second (B/s) and their multiples.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally fastest among registers, cache, RAM and secondary storage?

options.A: Registers, followed by CPU cache, main RAM and then secondary storage
options.B: Secondary storage, followed by RAM, cache and registers
options.C: RAM, followed by registers, secondary storage and cache

questions.explanation: Registers are generally fastest, followed by CPU cache, main RAM and then secondary storage. Exact performance depends on the specific technology and system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which memory is usually used as CPU cache?

options.A: SRAM, because it is fast and does not require periodic refresh while powered
options.B: DRAM, because it is slow and cheap

questions.explanation: SRAM is commonly used for CPU cache because it is fast and does not require periodic refresh while powered.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which memory is commonly used as main system RAM?

options.A: DRAM, including modern DDR SDRAM

questions.explanation: DRAM, including modern DDR SDRAM, is commonly used as main system memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which computer component connects the CPU, RAM and other major components?

options.A: The motherboard

questions.explanation: The motherboard provides the main physical and electrical connections among the CPU, RAM, storage and other components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which component executes program instructions?

options.A: The CPU

questions.explanation: The CPU executes program instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device converts printed documents into digital images?

options.A: A scanner

questions.explanation: A scanner converts printed documents or photographs into digital image data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which technology converts scanned printed text into editable machine-readable text?

options.A: OCR (Optical Character Recognition)

questions.explanation: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) converts recognised text in an image into machine-readable text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device detects shaded marks on objective answer sheets?

options.A: OMR (Optical Mark Recognition)

questions.explanation: OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) detects marked positions on specially designed forms.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which technology reads magnetic-ink characters on bank cheques?

options.A: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)

questions.explanation: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads characters printed using magnetic ink.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which printer uses toner?

options.A: A laser printer

questions.explanation: A laser printer uses toner, a fine powder, to form printed images on paper.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which storage device uses magnetic platters?

options.A: A hard disk drive (HDD)

questions.explanation: A hard disk drive (HDD) uses rotating magnetic platters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which storage device uses NAND flash memory?

options.A: SSDs, USB flash drives and memory cards

questions.explanation: SSDs, USB flash drives and memory cards commonly use NAND flash memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does HDMI stand for?

options.A: High-Definition Multimedia Interface

questions.explanation: HDMI stands for High-Definition Multimedia Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does SATA stand for?

options.A: Serial ATA, commonly expanded as Serial Advanced Technology Attachment

questions.explanation: SATA stands for Serial ATA, commonly expanded as Serial Advanced Technology Attachment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does SSD stand for?

options.A: Solid State Drive

questions.explanation: SSD stands for Solid State Drive.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does HDD stand for?

options.A: Hard Disk Drive

questions.explanation: HDD stands for Hard Disk Drive.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does GPU stand for?

options.A: Graphics Processing Unit

questions.explanation: GPU stands for Graphics Processing Unit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does PCIe stand for?

options.A: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express

questions.explanation: PCIe stands for Peripheral Component Interconnect Express.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does LED stand for?

options.A: Light-Emitting Diode

questions.explanation: LED stands for Light-Emitting Diode.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is an LED-backlit monitor the same as an OLED display?

options.A: No. An LED-backlit monitor is usually an LCD monitor with LED backlighting; OLED is a different self-emissive display technology
options.C: Yes, both use liquid crystals only
options.D: No, an LED monitor is a type of printer

questions.explanation: An LED-backlit monitor is usually an LCD monitor with LED backlighting; OLED is a different self-emissive display technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is the term 'CPU is the brain of the computer' a literal scientific fact?

options.A: No, it is a conventional exam analogy; the motherboard, memory, storage and input/output systems are also essential
options.B: Yes, the CPU is literally a biological brain
options.C: Yes, the CPU can think independently
options.D: No, the motherboard is the only brain

questions.explanation: The term 'CPU is the brain of the computer' is a conventional exam analogy. The motherboard, memory, storage and input/output systems are also essential.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the exam accuracy note say about hardware specifications?

options.A: Hardware specifications change over time; interface speeds, capacities and component designs vary by model, so one product's specification should not be treated as universal
options.D: Only software specifications change over time

questions.explanation: Hardware specifications change over time. Interface speeds, capacities and component designs vary by model; avoid treating one product's specification as universal.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is M.2 a synonym for NVMe?

options.A: No. M.2 is a form factor/connector family, not a synonym for NVMe; M.2 drives may use SATA or PCIe/NVMe
options.B: Yes, M.2 and NVMe are exactly the same
options.C: Yes, all M.2 drives are NVMe
options.D: No, M.2 is a type of printer

questions.explanation: M.2 is a form factor/connector family, not a synonym for NVMe. M.2 drives may use SATA or PCIe/NVMe.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is every ROM technology permanently unchangeable?

options.A: No. ROM is non-volatile, but PROM, EPROM and EEPROM have different programming and erasing characteristics
options.B: Yes, all ROM is permanently unchangeable
options.C: Yes, ROM can never be programmed

questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile, but not every ROM technology is permanently unchangeable. PROM, EPROM and EEPROM have different programming and erasing characteristics.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Where is modern firmware commonly stored?

options.A: In reprogrammable flash memory

questions.explanation: Modern firmware is commonly stored in reprogrammable flash memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a communication/networking device category of computer hardware?

options.A: Network interface card (NIC)

questions.explanation: The main categories of computer hardware include communication/networking devices. A network interface card (NIC) is an example of a networking device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a storage device?

options.A: Solid State Drive (SSD)

questions.explanation: A Solid State Drive (SSD) is a storage device. Monitor, keyboard and speaker are output/input devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a processing component?

options.A: CPU

questions.explanation: The CPU is a processing component. Monitor and printer are output devices; keyboard is an input device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a memory component?

options.A: RAM

questions.explanation: RAM is a memory component. Printer and monitor are output devices; scanner is an input device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an input device?

options.A: Scanner

questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device. Printer, speaker and projector are output devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an output device?

options.A: Monitor

questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device. Keyboard, scanner and mouse are input devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a specialised component found in modern processors besides ALU, CU and registers?

options.A: Caches, execution units and cores

questions.explanation: Modern processors also contain caches, execution units, cores and other specialised components, in addition to the ALU, CU and registers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which examples are given for multicore processors?

options.A: Dual-core, quad-core, hexa-core and octa-core

questions.explanation: Examples of multicore processors include dual-core, quad-core, hexa-core and octa-core processors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can a single-core processor run multiple programs?

options.A: Yes, through operating-system scheduling, although it does not have multiple CPU cores
options.B: No, it can run only one program ever
options.C: Yes, but only if it has NVMe storage
options.D: No, single-core processors cannot run an operating system

questions.explanation: A single-core processor can still run multiple programs through operating-system scheduling, but it does not have multiple CPU cores.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are DIMM slots called on many laptops?

options.A: SO-DIMM slots

questions.explanation: RAM slots are commonly called DIMM slots on desktop systems and SO-DIMM slots on many laptops.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: In modern computers, where are many functions once handled by a separate chipset integrated?

options.A: Into the CPU

questions.explanation: In modern computers, many functions once handled by a separate chipset are integrated into the CPU.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main modern expansion-slot standard for PCs?

options.A: PCI Express (PCIe)

questions.explanation: PCI Express (PCIe) is the main modern expansion-slot standard for PCs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Do modern PCs commonly use UEFI firmware instead of traditional BIOS?

options.A: Yes, modern PCs commonly use UEFI firmware, although the term BIOS is still widely used informally
options.B: No, modern PCs never use UEFI
options.C: No, modern PCs use only magnetic tape
options.D: Yes, but UEFI is a type of RAM

questions.explanation: Modern PCs commonly use UEFI firmware, although the term BIOS is still widely used informally.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which DDR generations are mentioned in the notes?

options.A: DDR, DDR2, DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5

questions.explanation: DDR generations include DDR, DDR2, DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5; they differ in speed, voltage, design and compatibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why are DDR4 and DDR5 modules not interchangeable?

options.A: They use different electrical and physical specifications
options.C: DDR4 is a type of printer
options.D: DDR5 is a type of optical disc

questions.explanation: DDR4 and DDR5 modules use different electrical and physical specifications and are not interchangeable in a motherboard slot.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is required for dual-channel memory to work?

options.A: Correct module placement and platform support

questions.explanation: Dual-channel memory is a memory configuration that uses two memory channels to increase the potential data bandwidth between the memory controller and RAM. Correct module placement and platform support are required.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is used in USB flash drives, memory cards, SSDs and many embedded devices?

options.A: Flash memory

questions.explanation: Flash memory is used in USB flash drives, memory cards, SSDs and many embedded devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which cache level may be divided into instruction cache and data cache?

options.A: L1 cache

questions.explanation: L1 (Level 1) cache is the smallest and generally fastest cache level, usually located within each CPU core. It may be divided into instruction cache and data cache.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which cache level is often shared by multiple CPU cores?

options.A: L3 cache

questions.explanation: L3 (Level 3) cache is generally larger than L1 and L2 and is often shared by multiple CPU cores, although exact designs vary by processor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which examples of spindle speeds are given in the notes?

options.A: 5,400 RPM or 7,200 RPM

questions.explanation: Spindle speed is measured in revolutions per minute (RPM), such as 5,400 RPM or 7,200 RPM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which part of an HDD moves the read/write head to the required track?

options.A: The actuator arm

questions.explanation: A typical HDD contains an actuator arm. Seek time is the time taken for the actuator to move the read/write head to the track containing the required data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which part of an HDD rotates the platters?

options.A: The spindle motor

questions.explanation: A typical HDD contains a spindle motor. Spindle speed is the rotational speed of the HDD platters, measured in RPM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the common form factor of a SATA SSD?

options.A: 2.5-inch drive form factor

questions.explanation: A SATA SSD connects through the Serial ATA interface, commonly using a 2.5-inch drive form factor. Its speed is limited by the SATA interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Over which interface does an NVMe SSD typically operate?

options.A: PCI Express (PCIe)

questions.explanation: An NVMe SSD uses the Non-Volatile Memory Express protocol, typically over PCI Express (PCIe), to communicate with flash storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the SSD controller manage?

options.A: Data placement, error correction, wear management and communication with the computer
options.B: Only the physical rotation of platters

questions.explanation: An SSD stores data electronically in NAND flash memory cells. A controller manages data placement, error correction, wear management and communication with the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How is NAND flash memory organised for reading, writing and erasing?

options.A: Into pages and blocks

questions.explanation: NAND flash stores data in cells and is organised into pages and blocks for reading, writing and erasing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which keys are examples of modifier keys on a keyboard?

options.A: Shift, Ctrl and Alt

questions.explanation: Common groups of keys include alphanumeric keys, function keys, modifier keys such as Shift/Ctrl/Alt, navigation keys, editing keys, arrow keys and the numeric keypad.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the accuracy of OCR dependent on?

options.A: Image quality and the text

questions.explanation: OCR accuracy depends on image quality and the text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which measurable human characteristics can a biometric input device capture?

options.A: Fingerprint, face pattern, iris pattern or voice

questions.explanation: A biometric input device captures a measurable human characteristic, such as a fingerprint, face pattern, iris pattern or voice, for identification or authentication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which physical conditions can a sensor detect as an input device?

options.A: Temperature, light, pressure, motion or humidity

questions.explanation: A sensor detects a physical condition, such as temperature, light, pressure, motion or humidity, and provides a signal that a computer or controller can process.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to image detail as screen resolution increases?

options.A: Higher resolution can provide more image detail, subject to screen size and content
options.B: Higher resolution always reduces image detail
options.C: Resolution has no effect on image detail
options.D: Higher resolution changes the colour of the image only

questions.explanation: Higher resolution can provide more image detail, subject to screen size and content.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does an LCD monitor control light?

options.A: Using liquid crystals to control light from a backlight or, in some designs, another illumination system
options.C: Using laser light on optical discs

questions.explanation: LCD stands for Liquid Crystal Display. An LCD uses liquid crystals to control light from a backlight or, in some designs, another illumination system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of impact printer?

options.A: Dot-matrix printer

questions.explanation: Examples of impact printers include dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers. Inkjet, laser and thermal printers are non-impact printers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-impact printer?

options.A: Laser printer

questions.explanation: A laser printer is a non-impact printer. Dot-matrix, daisy-wheel and line printers are impact printers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Where are thermal printers commonly used?

options.A: For receipts, labels and tickets

questions.explanation: A thermal printer is commonly used for receipts, labels and tickets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What technology may modern large-format plotters use?

options.A: Inkjet technology

questions.explanation: Modern large-format plotters may use inkjet technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which storage type is RAM classified as?

options.A: Primary storage

questions.explanation: Primary storage includes memory directly accessible by the CPU or closely integrated with processing, such as registers, cache and main memory (RAM).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which storage type is an HDD classified as?

options.A: Secondary storage

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile storage used to retain programs and data for long-term use, such as HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, memory cards and optical discs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which storage type involves automated tape systems for large-scale archival or backup?

options.A: Tertiary storage

questions.explanation: Tertiary storage is storage used for large-scale archival or backup purposes, often involving removable media libraries or automated tape systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of magnetic storage?

options.A: Hard disk drive and magnetic tape

questions.explanation: Magnetic storage records data by changing magnetic states on a medium. Examples include hard disk drives and magnetic tape.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of optical storage?

options.A: CD, DVD and Blu-ray Disc

questions.explanation: Optical storage uses laser light to read or write data on optical media. Examples include CD, DVD and Blu-ray Disc.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which common formats are used for memory cards?

options.A: SD and microSD

questions.explanation: Common memory card formats include SD and microSD.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a port used for connecting external devices?

options.A: USB port

questions.explanation: A port is a physical or logical connection point through which a computer communicates with another device. Examples of physical ports include USB, HDMI and Ethernet ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an expansion card?

options.A: Graphics card

questions.explanation: An expansion slot is a motherboard connector that allows an additional card, such as a graphics card, network card or sound card, to be installed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-volatile memory?

options.A: ROM

questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory because it retains stored contents without continuous electrical power.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a volatile memory?

options.A: Main system RAM

questions.explanation: Main system RAM is volatile memory, which means its contents are normally lost when power is switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which component is installed on a compatible motherboard?

options.A: CPU

questions.explanation: The CPU is installed on a compatible motherboard.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common PC motherboard form factor along with ATX?

options.A: microATX and Mini-ITX

questions.explanation: Common PC form factors include ATX, microATX and Mini-ITX.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which connector on the motherboard receives power from the PSU?

options.A: The motherboard power connector

questions.explanation: The motherboard power connector receives electrical power from the power supply unit (PSU) and distributes it through motherboard power circuitry to system components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What was traditionally maintained by the CMOS battery when the computer is unplugged?

options.A: The real-time clock and certain firmware settings

questions.explanation: The motherboard battery traditionally maintains the real-time clock and certain firmware settings when the computer is unplugged.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the full form of CMOS?

options.A: Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor

questions.explanation: CMOS originally refers to Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of secondary storage?

options.A: USB flash drive

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile storage used to retain programs and data for long-term use, such as HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, memory cards and optical discs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of primary storage?

options.A: Cache memory

questions.explanation: Primary storage is memory directly accessible by the CPU or closely integrated with processing, such as registers, cache and main memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common example of sequential-access storage?

options.A: Magnetic tape

questions.explanation: Sequential access means data are accessed in a sequence, where reaching a particular item may require passing earlier items. Magnetic tape is a common example.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following supports direct or random access?

options.A: RAM and disk-based storage

questions.explanation: Direct or random access means a storage system can access a specified location without reading all preceding locations. RAM and disk-based storage support direct access, although their access times differ.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does a data transfer rate measure?

options.A: The amount of data transferred per unit of time
options.B: The physical size of the storage device

questions.explanation: Data transfer rate is the amount of data transferred per unit of time, commonly expressed in bits per second (bps) or bytes per second (B/s) and their multiples.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is used to restore data after accidental deletion, corruption or hardware failure?

options.A: A backup

questions.explanation: A backup is a separate copy of data kept so that the data can be restored after accidental deletion, corruption, hardware failure, theft or another loss event.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common example of a peripheral device?

options.A: Printer

questions.explanation: A peripheral device is a hardware component connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions; examples include a keyboard, printer, external drive and scanner.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a communication/networking device category of computer hardware?

options.A: Modem

questions.explanation: The main categories of computer hardware include communication/networking devices. A modem is an example of a communication device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the role of the ALU in the CPU?

options.A: Performing arithmetic and logical/comparison operations

questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, and logical or comparison operations such as AND, OR, NOT, greater than and equality.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the Control Unit coordinate among?

options.A: The CPU, memory and input/output components
options.D: Only the hard disk and SSD

questions.explanation: The Control Unit fetches and decodes instructions and coordinates the movement of data and control signals among the CPU, memory and input/output components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about clock speed is correct?

options.A: Clock speed alone does not determine total performance
options.B: Higher clock speed always means a faster computer in every task
options.C: Clock speed is measured in gigabytes
options.D: Clock speed is the same as the number of instructions per second

questions.explanation: Clock speed alone does not determine total performance. A CPU's clock frequency is not the same as the number of instructions it completes per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a 64-bit architecture is correct?

options.A: It can address a much larger memory space than a 32-bit architecture, subject to operating-system and hardware limits
options.B: It can address less memory than a 32-bit architecture
options.C: It has no effect on memory addressing
options.D: It is only used in printers

questions.explanation: A 64-bit architecture can address a much larger memory space than a 32-bit architecture, subject to operating-system and hardware limits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is used with a heat sink to improve cooling?

options.A: A fan

questions.explanation: A heat sink is a passive cooling component, usually made of metal with fins, that transfers heat away from a processor or other component to the surrounding air. A fan may be used with it to improve cooling.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of thermal throttling?

options.A: Helping prevent overheating and damage by reducing performance when temperature becomes too high
options.B: Increasing processor speed when it gets hot

questions.explanation: Thermal throttling is the automatic reduction of a processor's operating frequency or performance when its temperature becomes too high, helping prevent overheating and damage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common motherboard feature?

options.A: Rear input/output ports and internal headers

questions.explanation: Common motherboard features include the CPU socket, RAM slots, chipset or platform controller, expansion slots, storage connectors, power connectors, firmware chip, rear input/output ports and internal headers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common storage connector found on a motherboard?

options.A: SATA connector

questions.explanation: Common motherboard features include storage connectors. SATA is a common storage connector. HDMI, USB and Ethernet are input/output ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a common use of an expansion slot?

options.A: Installing a graphics card, network card or sound card

questions.explanation: An expansion slot is a motherboard connector that allows an additional card, such as a graphics card, network card or sound card, to be installed. PCI Express (PCIe) is the main modern expansion-slot standard for PCs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that uses flash memory?

options.A: USB flash drive

questions.explanation: Flash memory is used in USB flash drives, memory cards, SSDs and many embedded devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an optical storage medium?

options.A: DVD

questions.explanation: Optical storage uses laser light to read or write data on optical media. Examples include CD, DVD and Blu-ray Disc.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc is correct?

options.A: It commonly stores 25 GB, more than a typical DVD or CD
options.D: It stores less than a CD

questions.explanation: A standard single-layer Blu-ray Disc commonly stores 25 GB, more than a typical DVD (4.7 GB) or CD (about 700 MB).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that functions as both input and output?

options.A: Touchscreen

questions.explanation: A touchscreen functions as both an input device and an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a graphics tablet used for?

options.A: Drawing or writing with a stylus and transferring the movements into digital form

questions.explanation: A graphics tablet is an input device that allows a user to draw or write with a stylus and transfer the movements into digital form.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that uses a light pen?

options.A: Older display technologies (largely obsolete)

questions.explanation: A light pen is a pen-shaped pointing device that detects its position on a compatible display. It was used with older display technologies and is largely obsolete.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that uses a laser or LED imaging system?

options.A: Laser printer

questions.explanation: A laser printer is a non-impact printer that uses an electro-photographic process, a laser or LED imaging system and toner to produce printed output.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that uses heat to create an image on heat-sensitive paper?

options.A: Thermal printer

questions.explanation: A thermal printer uses heat to create an image on heat-sensitive paper or to transfer ink from a ribbon. It is commonly used for receipts, labels and tickets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a device that uses an electro-photographic process?

options.A: Laser printer

questions.explanation: A laser printer is a non-impact printer that uses an electro-photographic process, a laser or LED imaging system and toner to produce printed output.
